command_ack_results_verification.method: Reconstructed by exact row position (row_number() over timestamp order), rows 751-892 of action_history - i.e. precisely the 142 rows that constitute the before(750)/after(892) delta reported in database_before_after.action_history. Sum of per-capability counts (8+121+6+4+3=142) matches the delta exactly by construction.
command_ack_results_verification.note: An earlier draft used an approximate calendar time-window query for the per-capability breakdown (LED=9, FAN=122, total=144), which did not exactly match the 142 before/after delta. This entry supersedes that draft; 142 is the correct, cross-checked figure used on every results asset.

command_dispatch_latency.metric: ACTION pipeline stage duration_ms (backend-side processing time to validate and dispatch a command)
command_dispatch_latency.source: pipeline_traces table, stage=ACTION, same validation window
command_dispatch_latency.distribution_note: Bimodal: a fast cluster (~5ms, n~89) and a slower cluster (~45-50ms, n~47), plausibly corresponding to rule-triggered SEND_COMMAND actions vs. the manually REST-dispatched Relay/Servo demo commands taking a different code path - not yet root-caused, reported as observed rather than fully explained.
command_dispatch_latency.excluded_metric_note: action_history.ack_received_at was deliberately NOT used for this measurement - it is set from the simulated device's own whole-second-truncated ACK payload timestamp (DeviceCommandAckMessageHandler.java, Instant.ofEpochSecond), not the backend's receipt time, so comparing it against the millisecond-precision dispatch timestamp produces meaningless (often negative) deltas. This is a real precision gap in that field, disclosed here rather than worked around silently.

ai_explanation_example.note: Deterministic fallback mode - not a claim of LLM-based inference; all FACT claims are grounded in persisted evaluation_evidence and action_history records.

known_limitation_observed_during_this_ru.description: Running the backend's own MQTT-related test suite concurrently with the live dev backend caused a client-ID collision on the shared local Mosquitto broker, wedging the dev backend's persistent MQTT session for a period and dropping outbound message delivery until manually cleared (reconnect with clean_session=true).
known_limitation_observed_during_this_ru.impact: No impact on the reported results - all reported evidence comes from a subsequent clean, uninterrupted validation run (20:07:12-20:11:22 UTC) captured after this was resolved.
known_limitation_observed_during_this_ru.recommendation: Run backend integration tests and the dev backend against separate MQTT broker instances, or not concurrently, in future sessions.
